claim: Sandakan was nicknamed 'Little Hong Kong of North Borneo' after British-encouraged Cantonese/Hakka migration built a dense shophouse port town.
quote: many Hong Kong traders eventually settled in Sandakan and in time the town was called the 'Little Hong Kong of North Borneo'

claim: Sandakan grew from the 1879 settlement; the pre-war town was totally destroyed by Allied bombing in 1944-45.
quote: As the war continued and Allied bombing started in 1944, the town was totally destroyed.

claim: William B. Pryer moved the administration on 21 June 1879 and named the new settlement 'Elopura', meaning beautiful city.
quote: Pryer named this place 'Elopura' meaning "beautiful city".

claim: The earlier Cowie settlement was renamed Kampong German for its German bases and burnt down accidentally on 15 June 1879.
quote: It was soon renamed Kampong German ... The Cowie settlement was accidentally burnt down on 15 June 1879.

claim: Sandakan's Little Hong Kong identity and trading-port backstory remain a live tourism narrative in 2026.
quote: Sandakan: Bah...you know the story or not?

claim: Pre-WWII Berhala Island was a quarantine station for labourers from China and the Philippines and home to a leper colony; Japan used it as an internment camp.
quote: the island was used as a quarantine station for labourers coming from China and the Philippines, and was also home to a leper colony.

claim: On 4 June 1943 the 'Berhala Eight' POWs escaped by taking a boat from the leper colony and paddling/sailing ~250km to Tawi-Tawi, missing the Sandakan Death Marches.
quote: McLaren, Kennedy, and Butler took a small boat from the leper colony and paddled across open ocean using wooden paddles ... saving the Eight from the notorious Sandakan Death Marches.

claim: Pulau Berhala, ~8km from Sandakan jetty, is being developed as a sustainable recreational-forest tourism site.
quote: Sandakan's Pulau Berhala, with its prominent cliffs and eventful history, is being developed as a sustainable tourism attraction.

claim: Australian and British POWs were held at the Sandakan camp during the Japanese occupation of Borneo.
quote: Australian POWs in Borneo

claim: Sandakan Memorial Park marks where ~2,400 Australian and British POWs died; entry is free.
quote: the death of approximately 2400 Australian and British prisoners of war held by the Japanese in the Sandakan POW camp

claim: Rusting WWII relics - an excavator, generator and boiler - still lie in their original positions at the former camp site.
quote: the rusting remains of an excavator and a generator and a boiler which still lie in their original positions near the steps leading up to a small Commemorative Pavilion.

claim: Between Jan-Jun 1945 over 1,000 POWs were force-marched 260km from Sandakan to Ranau; about half died en route.
quote: more than 1,000 malnourished POWs were force-marched to Ranau, 260 kilometres from Sandakan. About half died on the way.

claim: Masjid Jamek's timber pillars carry WWII bullet holes; land reclamation pushed the shoreline ~350m away and the heritage structure is now threatened by additions and landslide risk.
quote: visible bullet holes on pillars document combat ... land reclamation pushed Sandakan's edge approximately 350 meters further outward.

claim: Sandakan Jamek Mosque, the town's oldest mosque (opened 1890), was founded by Damsah, a Muslim cloth merchant from British India.
quote: the oldest mosque in Sandakan, opened in 1890 ... opened by Damsah, a Muslim cloth merchant from British Raj.

claim: St Michael's is Sabah's oldest stone church; white stone was imported from Hong Kong and the Japanese dynamited it before surrender in 1945, leaving the shell standing.
quote: The white stones ... were imported from Hong Kong ... The church was dynamited by the Japanese forces before surrender in 1945 ... although the shell of the church remained standing.

claim: St Michael's foundation stone was laid in 1893 and the church took over 30 years to complete.
quote: Our History - The Parish of St Michael and All Angels

claim: Agnes Keith House (the villa 'Newlands') was home to writer Agnes Keith and her husband Harry, Conservator of Forests, who popularised the phrase 'Land Below the Wind'.
quote: the story of American writer Agnes Keith and her British husband Harry, the Conservator of Forests in North Borneo, who lived in Sandakan from 1934 to 1952.

claim: Agnes Keith House is run as a heritage museum by the Sabah Museum department.
quote: Agnes Keith House, Sandakan | Sabah Museum

claim: The reconstructed bungalow displays period furniture, family photos and personal artefacts of the Keiths.
quote: A Charming Museum for a Remarkable Woman

claim: The English Tea House (opened 8 Dec 2002) sits in 1.5 acres of manicured lawn complete with a croquet pitch, beside Agnes Keith House overlooking Sandakan Bay.
quote: surrounded by 1.5 acres of manicured lawn, complete with a croquet pitch and outdoor seating.

claim: The English Tea House serves fine teas, scones and cream and English/Asian fare in a colonial setting.
quote: English Tea House & Restaurant Sandakan - fine dining Western cuisine in Sandakan

claim: The self-guided Sandakan Heritage Trail starts at the ~100-year-old Masjid Jamik and climbs the landmark 'Stairs with a Hundred Steps' to a hilltop viewpoint.
quote: begins at the 100-year-old Masjid Jamik mosque and includes climbing the Stairs with a Hundred Steps which lead to a beautiful view of Sandakan town and bay.

claim: Sam Sing Kung Temple (1887) venerates the 'Three Saints', holds 100 Taoist divination poems, and its bronze bell was donated by Sandakan's first Kapitan Cina, Fung Ming Shan.
quote: its original bronze bell was donated by Fung Ming Shan, Sandakan's first Kapitan Cina appointed by the British in 1887, the same year the temple was built.

claim: The 138-year-old temple was a religious centre for the Chinese labourers and merchants who earned Sandakan its 'Little Hong Kong' name.
quote: It formed a crucial religious centre for the thousands of Chinese labourers, farmers, and merchants ... earning Sandakan its 'Little Hong Kong' moniker.

claim: Hilltop Puu Jih Shih Temple (built 1987) at Tanah Merah has a seven-tiered pagoda and commanding views over Sandakan Bay.
quote: a Buddhist temple located at the hilltop of Tanah Merah at Sandakan Bay ... features a beautiful garden and a seven-tiered pagoda.

claim: Puu Jih Shih is one of Sandakan's best sunset-viewing spots, with the largest Chinese temple in town.
quote: One of Sandakan's best sunset viewing spots is from hilltop Puu Jih Shih Temple.

claim: Gomantong's caves (Simud Hitam and Simud Putih) are famous for edible swiftlet nests used in bird's-nest soup.
quote: The main cave system is divided into two parts: the more accessible Simud Hitam (Black Cave), and the larger Simud Putih (White Cave).

claim: Licensed collectors harvest nests twice a year using only rattan ladders, ropes and bamboo poles, under strict Sabah Wildlife Department quotas.
quote: locals with licenses climb to the roof of the caves, using only rattan ladders, ropes, and bamboo poles, and collect the nests.

claim: A swirling exodus of more than 2 million bats leaves Gomantong's cave mouth each evening, roughly 5:30-6:30pm.
quote: A swirling vortex of more than 2 million bats emerges from the cave mouth ... typically around 5:30 PM to 6:30 PM.

claim: The Rainforest Discovery Centre is a forest education park in the Kabili-Sepilok reserve near Sandakan.
quote: Rainforest Discovery Centre

claim: RDC has Sabah's longest canopy walkway (620m) and runs guided night walks (~RM30) to spot tarsiers, slow loris, civets and flying squirrels.
quote: the longest in Sabah ... During the highly recommended night walks (RM30) you may spot tarsiers, slow loris, civets, flying squirrels.

claim: The Bornean Sun Bear Conservation Centre rehabilitates the world's smallest bears; it houses ~41 rescued ex-captive sun bears.
quote: There are currently 41 rescued ex-captive sun bears residing at the BSBCC.

claim: Sun bears, found only in Southeast Asia, are the smallest bears on Earth and are classified Vulnerable.
quote: Sun bears are the smallest bears in the world and are only found in Southeast Asia.

claim: Labuk Bay's owner spared a 400-acre mangrove pocket from oil-palm clearance after discovering proboscis monkeys living there.
quote: the owner discovered that proboscis monkeys were living in the mangrove forest. He decided to retain this relatively small pocket of forest as a sanctuary.

claim: Labuk Bay Proboscis Monkey Sanctuary sits inside an oil-palm estate ~38km from Sandakan with scheduled feeding platforms.
quote: Labuk Bay Proboscis Monkey Sanctuary is located within an oil palm estate about 38 kilometres from Sandakan.

claim: Turtle Islands Park (40km north of Sandakan) lets overnight visitors watch a green turtle lay eggs at Selingan's hatchery; best March-October.
quote: Turtle landings usually occur after dusk, hence an overnight stay would be the best plan to see the turtles as they come ashore to lay their eggs.

claim: Evening mangrove cruises near Sandakan glide past riverbanks lit by thousands of fireflies, often with a seafood dinner.
quote: Sandakan River Cruise: Mangrove & Firefly Cruise

claim: Sandakan Crocodile Farm, 12km from town, is Malaysia's largest with ~3,000 crocodiles and a mini-zoo including a 100kg Amazonian fish.
quote: the largest among Malaysia's crocodile farms with over 3000 reptiles ... a mini zoo with a 100kg Amazonian fish.

claim: Sandakan's UFO tart - a biscuit base topped with custard and torched meringue - is locally called Cow Dung Tart (牛屎挞).
quote: Cow Dung Tart is also known as UFO Tart because of its flying saucer shape.

claim: The UFO tart was an accidental creation (scorched meringue) by Hainanese baker Fu Ah On in 1955; 5 May is 'UFO Tart Day'.
quote: UFO Tarts, Sandakan's Iconic Accidental Confection

claim: The three-storey Sandakan Central Market's signature local dish is dry kway teow with deep-fried pork.
quote: Don't leave without trying the dry Kway Teow with deep-fried pork. It's a local favorite!

claim: Sandakan's fish market is the biggest and busiest in Sabah, one of the state's most important seafood landing ports.
quote: The fish market here is perhaps the biggest and busiest in Sabah which offers a stunning array of fresh seafood.

claim: Buli Sim Sim is the original 1879 stilt settlement Sandakan grew from, reachable on foot by plank walkways ~3km east of town.
quote: the original settlement Sandakan grew from back in 1879 ... reachable by plank walkways.

claim: Buli Sim Sim has waterfront seafood restaurants, one a former fish market expanded into a floating restaurant.
quote: one of which was initially a fish market which was later expanded to include a floating seafood restaurant.

claim: Sandakan is wet year-round (~3,057mm/yr); rains ease April-June, while the NE monsoon brings >300mm/month Oct-Feb, peaking Nov-Dec.
quote: the rains decrease from April to June ... The rainiest period, with more than 300 mm (12 in) per month, is from October to February.

claim: March-May and July-August give Sandakan its driest, clearest weather for outdoor activities.
quote: the best time to visit Sandakan is March, April, May, July, and August, which offer drier weather.
